concept.title: The Date That Missed Its Reservation
concept.human_truth: Mature love does not remove childish irritation; it learns the feeling beneath it and still finds a way back to play.
concept.emotional_arc: playful departure -> small irritation -> respectful pause -> disappointment understood -> accidental roadside date -> affectionate callback

slides.copy:
This is the kind of love
I want us to grow into.
slides.visual: Rain-damp evening beside a tiny roadside chai stall. Exactly Aachu and Zuv stand under one umbrella beside their modest dark car, safely parked on the quieter service lane away from traffic, dressed for a proper date. Across the divided road, through moving cars, the intended restaurant on the next road is visibly close but inconvenient to reach. The chai stall glows immediately beside them. Aachu points toward the chai stall with her right hand while her left hand stays relaxed at her side. Zuv holds the umbrella in his right hand and lowers the phone map in his left; they exchange a small conspiratorial 'shall we?' look. This is the decision before the accidental date, not the seated payoff. No chai vendor or background people visible.
slides.emotion: rainy frustration turning into a shared mischievous decision
slides.props: one umbrella, one modest dark parked car, lowered phone map, glowing chai stall, distant restaurant frontage across divided road
slides.continuity_lock: Same date-night wardrobe, same modest dark car, same umbrella, and same rainy evening continue through slides 2-7. Exactly two visible people in every frame. No scooter or helmets.
slides.cta_intent: Send this as: this is the kind of love I want us to grow into.

The date began with one missing key
and two suspects.

slides.copy:
By the third wrong turn,
nobody was cute anymore.
slides.visual: They stand beside their modest dark car, safely parked on the quieter service lane of a rain-slick divided road. A phone map in Zuv's hand reroutes while the intended restaurant is frustratingly visible across the traffic on the next road. Aachu holds the closed umbrella downward and looks away toward the restaurant, tired and irritated; Zuv studies the route with restrained frustration. Exactly two visible people and no human reflections.

slides.copy:
“Don’t talk to me.”

He gave her the minute.
Not the distance.
slides.visual: At a safe recessed roadside edge near their parked dark car, Aachu faces slightly away with arms folded. Zuv stays beside the car several feet behind her, body open and grounded, not reaching or crowding. His phone hangs lowered at his side; the closed umbrella leans securely against the car. The empty space between them communicates a respected pause while his remaining nearby communicates care. Exactly two people.

slides.copy:
It wasn’t really the wrong turn.

They had simply missed each other
for too many ordinary days.

Their body distance has narrowed but they do not yet touch. Exactly two people, no background diners or staff.

slides.copy:
The plan failed.
The date didn’t.
slides.visual: At the tiny roadside chai stall beside their safely parked dark car, Aachu steals a sip from Zuv's chai after finishing hers. The glass is visibly at her own lips, not being offered to him. Zuv gives her a mock-offended look while protecting the biscuit packet against his chest. Two stools are now pulled close. The unreachable restaurant glows softly across the divided road behind traffic. Exactly two people, vendor out of frame.

slides.copy:
He still checked the lock twice.
She still rolled her eyes.

Then she went back
and checked it with him.
slides.visual: Nonlinear callback before departure, entirely OUTSIDE the apartment in a dry corridor. Medium-wide, nearly straight-on full-body view. The fully closed door is centered; its single exterior lever handle is on the RIGHT edge beside Zuv. The halfway-closing elevator and glowing call button are on frame left behind Aachu. Exactly two people stand on one depth plane, almost equal in apparent height, Zuv only slightly taller. Aachu stands on the door's left half and Zuv immediately beside its handle on the right, with one forearm of empty space between their torsos: no touch, lean on each other, hug, waist hold, or overlap. Both lower bodies still aim left toward the elevator while their upper bodies turn back to the door. Zuv's uncovered LEFT arm stays continuous from shoulder to five visible fingers wrapped around the exterior lever; the lever angles down under clear pulling/testing tension. His RIGHT arm and hand remain hidden behind his own back, never crossed or pocketed. Aachu turns back from the elevator to the door: her left foot points to the elevator, her lifted right heel steps back to the apartment, and three tiny fading graphite motion ticks show that return path from elevator threshold to heel. She performs a clearly forceful push-test on the closed center-left panel, well away from Zuv's handle hand: her visible RIGHT palm lies flat, her elbow is locked straight, her shoulder and upper torso lean their weight into that arm, the shirt sleeve compresses at the shoulder, and two tiny graphite pressure ticks touch the panel beside her palm. Her whole right arm stays continuously readable. Her left hand stays hidden by the tote on her shoulder and tightly rolled dry umbrella under her arm. Zuv looks at his handle grip and Aachu looks at her palm contact; neither looks at the other or viewer. Both smile slightly. Aachu: real soft oval face, mostly straight long dark hair, white shirt, blue jeans, red flats. Zuv: real broader face, swept wavy quiff not ringlets, trimmed beard, light blue shirt, loose grey trousers, red-black shoes. Clothes, shoes, umbrella, hair, and floor are pristine and dry. Both participate in one functional push-pull check through two separate simultaneous contacts: he flexes the handle outward while she pushes the closed panel inward after going back.
